items.title: الكرة الذهبية تكشف مفاجأة جديدة.. أين حل ميسي في تصويت البرتغال؟
items.summary: تصويت يثير الجدل
items.body: تصويت يثير الجدل كشف تصويت الصحفي البرتغالي أنطونيو تاديا في جائزة الكرة الذهبية لعام 2026 عن اختيارات لافتة، بعدما منح صدارة قائمته للإسباني لامين يامال، متجاهلًا وضع الفائز بالجائزة هاري كين في مركز متقدم، ومفضلًا عليه عددًا من النجوم، بينما جاء الأرجنتيني ليونيل ميسي في المركز السابع. ووضع تاديا نجم برشلونة الشاب في المرتبة الأولى، يليه الفرنسي كيليان مبابي، ثم النرويجي إيرلينج هالاند، فيما احتل الجورجي خفيتشا كفاراتسخيليا المركز الرابع، وجاء الإسباني باو كوبارسي خامسًا، بينما اكتفى كين بالمركز السادس، متقدمًا بمركز واحد على ميسي. ولم تتوقف المفاجآت عند هذا الحد، إذ ضمت القائمة البرتغالي نونو مينديز في المركز الثامن، والأرجنتيني لاوتارو مارتينيز تاسعًا، والإسباني رودري عاشرًا، في تصويت عكس تفضيلات الصحفي البرتغالي بشأن أبرز نجوم الموسم. وعلى مستوى الحضور البرتغالي في الترتيب النهائي، جاء فيتينيا في المركز الرابع عشر برصيد 59 نقطة، ليكون أفضل لاعبي بلاده، تلاه جواو نيفيز في المركز التاسع عشر بـ15 نقطة، ثم نونو مينديز في المركز الثالث والعشرين بـ8 نقاط، وبرونو فرنانديز في المركز السابع والعشرين بـ5 نقاط.

items.title: Soulframe opens up for everyone next week as the Warframe devs prepare the fantasy action RPG for one of its 'biggest, most violent' updates ever next month
items.summary: Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it's easier for new players to follow.
items.body: After three years of invite-only playtests, Soulframe is opening its doors to everyone next week on November 6. If you've been waiting to see what the developers of Warframe are doing with a fantasy action RPG, you'll finally be able to jump in and see for yourself. The transition to an open alpha will be followed by a massive transformation to the structure of the game later in November. Midrath, Soulframe's big open landmass, won't be the verdant, almost chill, place it used to be: The entire area will be corrupted and it's your job to bring it back to life. "You're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance," creative director Geoff Crookes explained in a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer. This update, Prelude 17 or Verse of the Veillands, is a huge shift for Soulframe, but an important one that will help new players acclimate to the world. Crookes said the goal is to improve the onboarding experience and to give players "much more ownership" over their decisions early on. items.body: Yesterday, the world received the sad news that legendary stage and screen actor Patrick Stewart had died at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia." His passing has triggered an internet-wide celebration of his life—particularly from Star Trek fans honoring his tenure as The Next Generation's Captain Jean-Luc Picard. While countless social media posts have already been penned in Stewart's memory, a subset of Trekkies are grieving together in the shared virtual spaces of Star Trek Online, the modest MMO that's still keeping the lights on 16 years after its 2010 launch. items.body: Fallout 4's overworld was always missing something that the other 3D wastelands in the series offered me: a sense of bleakness and danger. There are areas of the map, like the Glowing Sea, that managed to dial up the oppression. But the unforgiving horror mod Whispering Hills makes the whole region eerie and mysterious. And I honestly love that. Presented by (Image credit: Torn Banner) This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 . My playthrough started the same way as vanilla Fallout 4, with a tableau of mid-Century suburban domestic bliss interrupted by a tense run to Vault 111. But from there, I almost started to think my hard drive was haunted. The post-nuclear world has been reimagined with constant, dense fog and occasional torrential rain that limit your view distance to only a handful of yards. It reminded me of how Morrowind used its limited view distance to make Vvardenfell feel much bigger than it was, even if at the time it was also a technical necessity. items.body: In the world of wireless gaming headsets, there's one spec that draws me in like a moth to a flame: battery life. Particularly 100-hour+ battery life. items.body: World of Warcraft: Forever is "realmless", which has a couple of advantages for oceanic (OCE) players—who so often get the short end of the stick when it comes to MMORPGs. Blizzard has servers in Australia, so OCE players can enjoy not having terrible ping, but due to the smaller playerbase they share a lot of overlap with the North American server architecture. Which produces a unique problem: As it stands, OCE players are stuck in perpetual night. See, Forever has a 24 hour day/night cycle, so if you play during the evening and your timezone's matched to the server, the sun will set in Azeroth roughly at the time it would outside your window. But since OCE players are very much not local to North America… the curse of endless night persists. The culprit, of course, was AI. A Google search that once might have led someone to a 14-year-old Reddit thread containing the answer to a rare household cleaning problem is now likely to present that answer in an AI summary, no click required. That, Dyack believes, has shifted expectations for early access releases overall, and made life more difficult for indie developers who rely on the process to actually get their games finished and launched. "They can put up a polished product and rake in cash," Dyack told GamesIndustry . "It's a marketing beat for them. items.body: In this week's 'what the memory crisis is doing to people' news, a YouTuber has recently bought 32 GB of DDR5 laptop memory online and successfully converted it into memory for their desktop. Overall, it cost them just $175 ($120 for the memory and $55 for extra components). That's a bit of a bargain, as 32 GB DDR5 dual-channel memory is fetching upwards of $500 on Newegg right now. Blighted Agent took to their YouTube channel to share the process, where they purchased two SO-DIMM sticks of 16 GB DDR5 memory on Facebook Marketplace (presumably salvaged from a dead laptop). From here, they put a stick on a preheater, then removed the BIOS chip, the SPD chip and all eight of its memory chips. Buying new DDR5 DIMM PCBs and heatsinks off AliExpress, they cleaned the factory unleaded solder on the laptop memory, then soldered them onto the new PCBs. It's an impressive feat that requires reballing the memory chips with a stencil, a very precise procedure. Blighted Agent says, "You want a thin layer of flux, not too much or not too little.
